guidePage.title: Guide
guidePage.metaDescription: TwiCa usage guide. Learn how to use TwiCa as a viewer or streamer.

step1.title: Use Channel Points in Stream
step1.description: Watch a TwiCa-enabled stream and redeem the card gacha using channel points. Use the channel point redemption set up by the streamer (e.g., "Card Gacha"). You can draw gacha even without logging in to TwiCa.

step2.title: Get Cards
step2.description: When you draw gacha, you'll randomly receive original cards created by the streamer. Your acquired card will also appear on stream. Even without logging in, your gacha results are automatically saved to your Twitch account.

step3.title: Login with Twitch (To View Collection)
step3.description: To view your card collection, you need to log in to TwiCa. Click the "Login with Twitch" button on the homepage to log in with your Twitch account.

step4.title: View Your Collection
step4.description: After logging in, check your acquired cards in "My Collection" on your dashboard. Statistics by rarity are also displayed.

streamer.title: For Streamers
streamer.requirement: * Using streamer features requires that Twitch channel points are available on your channel. Thanks to Twitch's "Monetization for All", Affiliate or Partner status is not required — channel points become available once monetization onboarding and Channel Points are set up in your Twitch Creator Dashboard. In that case you can still use streamer features by enabling them with the steps below.

step1.title: Login with Twitch
step1.description: Log in to TwiCa with your Twitch account. Affiliate and Partner accounts have streamer features enabled automatically at login, so the next step is not needed.

step2.title: Enable Streamer Features (Non-Affiliate/Partner)
step2.description: If you are not an Affiliate or Partner, enable streamer features with the steps below. Enabling this unlocks card management, overlays, and reward settings.
step2.substep1: Open "User Settings" from the gear icon at the top right and find the "Channel Points / Streamer Features" section.
step2.substep2: If additional permission is requested, click "Re-link with Twitch to check" and allow reading and managing channel point redemptions.
step2.substep3: Once it says "We confirmed Channel Points are available on Twitch for your channel", click "Enable streamer features on twica".

step3.title: Create Cards
step3.description: Create original cards from "Card Management" on your dashboard. Set card name, image, rarity, and drop rate.

step4.title: Set Up Channel Point Redemption
step4.description: Select or create a channel point redemption from "Stream Settings" on your dashboard. Click "Save & Register EventSub" to complete the Twitch integration.

step5.title: Add Overlay to OBS
step5.description: Copy the OBS browser source URL shown in "Stream Settings" and add it as a browser source in OBS. Recommended size is 800x600. Gacha results will then appear on your stream.

step6.title: Start Streaming
step6.description: Once you start streaming, viewers can draw card gacha using channel points. Acquired cards automatically appear on your stream.

tips.title: Tips
tips.tip1: Drop rates are set using "weight". The actual probability is the ratio of each card's weight to the total weight of all cards.
tips.tip2: You can temporarily exclude cards from gacha by setting them to "Paused".
tips.tip3: Uploaded images can be cropped to Square (800x800) or Portrait (800x1118). Images specified by URL are used as-is without cropping.
tips.tip4: Make sure EventSub status shows "Connected" before starting your stream.
tips.tip5: If you see "Channel Points are not currently available on Twitch for this channel", confirm that monetization onboarding and Channel Points are set up in your Twitch Creator Dashboard, then try "Recheck".
tips.tip6: If streamer menu items do not appear after you enable streamer features, log out and log back in to refresh your session.

faqPage.title: FAQ
faqPage.metaDescription: Frequently asked questions about TwiCa. Learn the basics for viewers, streamers, and troubleshooting.
faqPage.intro: Common questions about using TwiCa are collected here. For full setup steps, also check the guide page.

login.question: Do I need to log in to draw gacha?
login.answer: No. You can draw gacha from a TwiCa-enabled stream's channel point redemption without logging in to TwiCa. Twitch login is required to view your collection.

collection.question: Where can I see cards I received?
collection.answer: After logging in with Twitch, open My Collection from the dashboard. Gacha results are saved to your Twitch account.

missingCards.question: What should I do if cards do not appear?
missingCards.answer: First confirm that the Twitch account you logged in with is the same account that drew the gacha. If it still does not appear, reload the page after a short wait.

affiliate.question: Are there requirements for streamer features?
affiliate.answer: The requirement is that channel point redemptions are available on your Twitch channel. Thanks to Twitch's "Monetization for All", Affiliate or Partner status is not required — channel points become available once monetization onboarding and Channel Points are set up in the Twitch Creator Dashboard. Affiliate and Partner accounts are enabled automatically at login; everyone else can enable streamer features from User Settings.

enableStreamer.question: I am not an Affiliate or Partner. How do I enable streamer features?
enableStreamer.answer: Open "User Settings" from the gear icon at the top right and find the "Channel Points / Streamer Features" section. If additional permission is requested, click "Re-link with Twitch to check" and allow reading and managing channel point redemptions. Once it is confirmed as available, click "Enable streamer features on twica" to unlock card management, overlays, and reward settings.

setup.question: What should I set up first?
setup.answer: Create cards, select or create a channel point redemption in Stream Settings, then save and register EventSub.

overlay.question: What should I add to OBS?
overlay.answer: Copy the OBS browser source URL shown in Stream Settings and add it as a browser source in OBS. The recommended size is 800x600.

cards.question: How are card drop rates decided?
cards.answer: Drop rates are based on each card's weight. A card's chance is its weight divided by the total weight of all cards currently included in gacha.

eventsub.question: Gacha does not run after a channel point redemption
eventsub.answer: Check the EventSub status in Stream Settings. If it is not connected, save and register it again. Also confirm that the channel point redemption is enabled on Twitch.

channelPointsUnavailable.question: It says Channel Points are not available on Twitch
channelPointsUnavailable.answer: Channel points are not available on your Twitch channel yet. Complete monetization onboarding and turn on Channel Points in your Twitch Creator Dashboard, then try "Recheck" in User Settings.

capabilityLost.question: Streamer features are enabled, but it says Channel Points actions require re-authorization or a recheck
capabilityLost.answer: This appears when your Twitch permissions or Channel Points status changed. If the additional permission was removed, open Stream Settings — a re-link button appears there so you can re-link with Twitch. If Channel Points became unavailable on Twitch, restore the settings in your Twitch Creator Dashboard, then reopen User Settings after 24 hours and it is rechecked automatically. Card management, Stream Settings and the rest of the streamer features remain available.

imageUpload.question: Image upload fails
imageUpload.answer: Check the file type, file size, and image aspect ratio. If the image is too large, compress it and try uploading again.

support.question: Where should I ask if the issue is not resolved?
support.answer: Contact the operator through the social links or contact details on the About page. Streamer name, operation details, and time of occurrence help with investigation.

article1.title: Article 1: Information We Collect
article1.intro: The Service collects the following information:
article1.item1: Twitch account information (user ID, username, display name, profile image URL)
article1.item2: Twitch authentication credentials (access tokens and refresh tokens required for OAuth)
article1.item3: Service usage data (gacha history, card collection data, Terms of Service acceptance timestamp)
article1.item4: Access data (page view analytics via Cloudflare Web Analytics)

article3.title: Article 3: Third-Party Services
article3.intro: The Service uses the following third-party services. Please refer to each service's privacy policy for their handling of personal information.
article3.item1: Twitch (authentication and API integration) - subject to the Twitch Privacy Notice
article3.item2: Cloudflare (hosting and Web Analytics) - subject to the Cloudflare Privacy Policy
article3.item3: Supabase (database and personal data storage; data is stored on servers outside Japan) - subject to the Supabase Privacy Policy

article4.title: Article 4: Use of Cookies
article4.content: The Service uses cookies to maintain login sessions and save language preferences. These cookies are essential for the basic functionality of the Service and are not used for third-party cookies or advertising-based tracking.

article5.title: Article 5: Information Sharing and Disclosure
article5.intro: The Service does not share collected personal information with third parties, except in the following cases:
article5.item1: When required by law to disclose information
article5.item2: When providing information to third-party services (as described in Article 3) to the extent necessary for service operations

article6.title: Article 6: Data Retention and Your Rights
article6.content: Collected information is retained for as long as necessary to provide the Service. You have the right to request disclosure, correction, suspension of use, or deletion of your personal information. To exercise these rights, please contact us through the About page.

article7.title: Article 7: Changes to This Policy
article7.content: The operator may modify this Policy at any time. Modified Policy takes effect when posted on the Service.

usagesPage.title: Fun ways to use TwiCa!
usagesPage.metaDescription: Looking for card ideas? From topic decks to fan art, here are fun ways to use TwiCa cards.
usagesPage.lead: Cards are not just for gacha and collections. Try these ideas to make your streams even more fun!

topicDeck.title: Topic deck
topicDeck.description: Create themed cards around your stream topics and get your viewers excited together.
topicDeck.example: Examples: moments from your stream, trending topics, event themes

foodDiary.title: What you ate today
foodDiary.description: Turn your daily meals into cards. Share a "food diary" with viewers and aim for completion.
foodDiary.example: Examples: today's lunch, favorite cafés, new convenience store finds

acquaintanceStreamers.title: Fellow streamers
acquaintanceStreamers.description: Turn streamers you know into cards. Use collections to spark collaboration and community.
acquaintanceStreamers.example: Examples: streamer friends, collab partners, streamers you follow

quoteCards.title: Quote cards
quoteCards.description: Turn legendary lines and memorable moments from your streams into cards. Your record becomes a collection.
quoteCards.example: Examples: famous stream moments, signature catchphrases, legendary fails

fanArt.title: Fan art
fanArt.description: Turn fan art drawn by your viewers into cards. Share the joy of seeing their work become a collection.

favoritePlaces.title: Favorite places & travel
favoritePlaces.description: Turn your favorite places and travel destinations into cards. Collect the places you want to visit.
favoritePlaces.example: Examples: great places you've been, dream destinations, local landmarks

getStarted.title: Getting started
getStarted.description: See the usage guide for details on creating cards and setting them up on your stream.
